records.title: City of Avondale FY2027 Final Adopted Budget
records.text: RESOLUTION NO. 1041-0626 A RESOLUTION OF THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AVONDALE, ARIZONA, SETTING FORTH THE FINAL BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-2027. WHEREAS, pursuant to the provisions of the laws of the State of Arizona and the City Charter, the Council of the City of Avondale (the “City Council’) is required to adopt an annual budget for the City of Avondale (the “City”); and WHEREAS, in accordance with ARIZ. REV. STAT. § 42-17102, the City Manager prepared and filed with the City Council the City Manager’s Budget estimates for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027; and WHEREAS, on May 4, 2026 the City Council approved Resolution 1029-0526, adopting (i) an expenditure limitation and (ii) the estimates of expenditures for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, and ending June 30, 2027, as the tentative budget for the City; and WHEREAS, Resolution 1029-0526 also directed the City Manager or designee to: (i) publish in the official City newspaper once per week for two consecutive weeks, (a) the official tentative budget and (b) a notice of the public hearing of the City Council to hear taxpayers and make tax levies at designated times and places; and (ii) not later than seven business days following consideration of Resolution 1029-0526 by the City Council, (a) make available at the Avondale Civic Center Library, the Sam Garcia Western Avenue Library and the Avondale City Hall a complete copy of the tentative budget, and (b) post the tentative budget on the City’s website; and WHEREAS, due notice has been given by the City Clerk as required by law that the City Council would meet on June 1, 2026, at the City Council Chambers for the purposes (i) hearing taxpayers on the proposed expenditures and proposed tax levies as set forth in the estimates and (11) adopting the tentative budget as final; and WHEREAS, on June 1, 2026, the City Council held a public hearing on the final budget as required by law; and WHEREAS, the City of Avondale Procurement Code 25-6 specificies that budgeted line items approved by the City Council in the review and adoption of the annual budget of the City, and for which an award is within the allocated expenditure, may be approved by the procurement agent or authorized designee.

records.title: City of Avondale FY2027 Final Adopted Budget
records.text: NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AVONDALE as follows: SECTION 1. The recitals above are hereby incorporated as if fully set forth herein. SECTION 2. The statements and schedules hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference are hereby formally adopted as the official final budget for the City for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027. SECTION 3. The statements and schedules hereto as Exhibit B and incorporated herein by reference are hereby identified as specifically budgeted line items greater than $100,000 for the City of Avondale, Arizona for the fiscal year July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. SECTION 4. The statements and schedules hereto as Exhibit C and incorporated herein by reference are hereby identified as the scheduled Interfund Transfers and scheduled Interfund Loans for the City of Avondale, Arizona for the fiscal year July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. SECTION 5. The statements and schedules hereto as Exhibit D and incorporated herein by reference are hereby identified as the Capital Improvement Plan for the City of Avondale, Arizona for the fiscal year July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. SECTION 6. Upon the recommendation by the City Manager and with approval of the City Council, transfers of appropriation from the non-departmental contingencies are permissible. SECTION 7. Money from any fund may be used for any of these appropriations except money specifically restricted by State Law, City Ordinance, City Council action or City Charter. SECTION 8. If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, phrase or portion of this Resolution or any part of the statements and schedules or fee schedule incorporated herein by reference are for any reason to be held invalid or unconstitutional by the decision of any court of competent jurisdiction, such decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions thereof. SECTION 9. The Mayor, the City Manager, the City Clerk and the City Attorney are hereby authorized and directed to take all steps necessary to carry out the purpose and intent of this Resolution. [SIGNATURES ON FOLLOWING PAGE]

records.text: Title: |§ Annual Racketeering Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Department: Police (RICO) Fund Appropriations Priority: FTEs 0 Reason: Program Enhancement Request Type: Supplemental Requests Published: Yes Sub Type: Variable Adjustment Stage: CMO Approved IT Reviewed? 3 -NA HR Reviewed? 3-NA Ongoing: $0 One-Time: $800,000 Total: $800,000 Council Goal: © Community Well-Being Description: This request is to appropriate annual spending authority of Racketeering Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) funds. The RICO Act is a US federal law enacted in 1970 to combat organized crime. It allows prosecutors to charge individuals or groups involved in ongoing criminal enterprises, rather than prosecuting isolated crimes. Under RICO, law enforcement can target patterns of illegal activity such as fraud, bribery, drug trafficking, money laundering, extortion, and other coordinated criminal conduct. One of RICO's most powerful features is its asset forfeiture provision. If a person or organization is convicted under RICO, the government can seize assets connected to the criminal enterprise. These assets can include cash, real estate, vehicles, bank accounts, and other property derived from or used in illegal activity. The use of forfeiture funds must follow federal, state, and local laws, as well as internal accountability standards. Transparency, oversight, and ethical safeguards are important to ensure funds are used appropriately and do not create improper incentives. Ongoing: $0 One-Time: $0 Total: $0 Council Goal: © Community Well-Being Description: Drone as First Responder (DFR), consists of a drone that is housed in a fully enclosed docking station that is affixed to the rooftop of a building. The drones are automated and able to be deployed by a trained employee to any call for service within a very short time period. They allow for immediate and accurate information to be relayed to responding officers. These drones are flown at a maximum height of 200ft unless a radar is used in which they can be flown as high as 400ft. The average distance for a DFR ranges from 2 to 3.5 miles and can reach speeds up to 50 MPH. On average the drone may be deployed for approximately 45 minutes depending on the distance, speed, and other factors. Justification: The Avondale Police Department currently has a drone program which consists of 16 drones, these drones are assigned to officers who have completed the required training through the FAA and have received their drone pilots license. This program requires a drone officer to be on duty and available to respond to the scene and deploy the drone from their vehicle, it also requires a trained observer to be present with the drone officer. With the DFR program, the drone would be able to immediately be launched and respond directly to the scene of the incident, responding much faster than an officer in a vehicle most of the time. The information obtained from the DFR would be in real time and first hand information obtained from the DFR pilot. This immediate and accurate information is critical to responding officers, their safety and their ability to understand what they are responding to. The DFR pilot is also able to send a link to responding officers or supervisors that would allow them to see exactly what the DFR pilot is seeing, allowing for a safe response. The DFR would allow for responding officers to have direct information on potential weapons involved, the number of individuals involved and their location, etc. Expenditures: Fund Category Display Name Ongoing One-Time Total 1010 - General Fund 6000 - Contractual Services - - Total 18

records.title: City of Avondale FY2027 City Manager's Recommended Budget
records.text: The police department implemented crime center cameras within the city’s boundaries in 2023. We currently have 15 cameras strategically placed throughout the McDowell Road and Van Buren Street areas. This has allowed all officers to gain access to the database, which includes the camera system of 141 law enforcement agencies throughout the country. By implementing this program with just 15 cameras, our officers have been able to solve multiple crimes in our city, and have also used the system to strengthen investigations. Our officers use the database to help with their investigations in which a vehicle may be involved in. Our Criminal Investigations Bureau and Special Investigations Bureau, utilizes the system as part of their case building, which has yielded in vital information being obtained. The following section contains just a few of the many success stories our officers have had using the cameras: In June of 2024, the Community Action Team (CAT Team), utilized the cameras to identify two vehicles involving two suspects connected to a public sexual indecency investigation at a city park. This subsequently led to charges being filed against both suspects. In August of 2024, the CAT Team utilized the cameras to identify a suspect vehicle and suspect involved in an organized retail theft spanning several cities. This investigation resulted in the apprehension and arrest of multiple suspects in a $22,000 dollar case. In September of 2024, the CAT Team also utilized the cameras to track a suspect vehicle for a suspect who had committed theft of over $200,000 over an extended period of time to a local grocery store chain spanning several cities. CAT was able to arrest the suspect in this matter. In December of 2024, the cameras were utilized to track a suspect vehicle involved in copper thefts of a housing development in south Avondale. Officers were able to arrest two suspects responsible for the crime. In March of 2025, the cameras were utilized by the Street Crimes Unit, in conjunction with an ongoing investigation regarding an international drug sales case which led to arrests and large amounts of drugs being recovered. In May of 2025, the cameras were utilized to help piece together a series of vehicle burglaries, vehicle thefts and weapons misconduct. Officers were able to use the cameras to track vehicles involved in the incidents which provided evidence for the arrest of a suspect. The rest of our city would immensely benefit with an addition of 58 cameras throughout all portions of the city where no cameras are currently placed. By increasing the number of cameras in our city, we would multiply the effectiveness of these cameras to help solve crimes such as vehicle burglaries, major crimes and also strengthen investigations. The system enables real-time information sharing and seamless interagency collaboration by allowing participating agencies to quickly search, access, and exchange critical records across jurisdictions. Justification: The need for this platform is significant. Our current systems operate independently, creating delays, inefficiencies, and limitations when attempting to share information with neighboring agencies. As criminal activity frequently, and quickly, crosses municipal boundaries, the inability to easily access each other's records can hinder investigations, slow response times, and impact officer safety. This program resolves these challenges by standardizing data and centralizing access, while still allowing each agency to control what information is shared. This platform is already being adopted across the region, including many of West Valley agencies including Phoenix, Glendale, Buckeye, Goodyear, Peoria, MCSO, and DPS. Moving forward alongside these agencies ensures we maintain full interoperability and are positioned to benefit from the same regional intelligence sharing as our West Valley Police agency counterparts. records.text: Title: | Redaction Software for Body Worn Cameras (BWC) Department: Police Priority: 07 FTEs 0 Reason: Program Enhancement Request Type: Supplemental Requests Published: Yes Sub Type: Stage: CMO Approved IT Reviewed? 1 - Yes HR Reviewed? 3-NA Ongoing: $25,000 One-Time: $0 Total: $25,000 Council Goal: — Innovative and Effective Government Description: A redaction secure, cloud-based tool within the platform that enables the Department to efficiently process public records and legal disclosure requests involving digital evidence. The software allows authorized personnel to accurately redact sensitive information—such as faces, license plates, personal identifiers, and protected locations—from body-worn camera footage, in-car video, and other digital media prior to release. A redaction that streamlines compliance with public records laws by reducing manual processing time, minimizing the risk of inadvertent disclosure, and ensuring consistent, auditable redaction practices. Integration within a platform that allows redactions to be applied without altering original evidence files, preserving evidentiary integrity while supporting transparency, legal compliance, and the timely fulfillment of records requests. Justification: The Department's current redaction tools require manual, frame-by-frame editing for most forms of redaction and do not include any Al- assisted functionality. As a result, redacting specific elements such as faces, license plates, or other sensitive information is extremely time- consuming and labor-intensive. In many cases, the only practical option available under the system is the application of a full-frame or full- media blur, which can unnecessarily obscure relevant content and reduce the usefulness of the released material. The volume of public records requests involving body-worn camera footage and digital imagery continues to rise, placing a significant strain on staff resources and extending turnaround times. The limitations of the current redaction process extend the time required to complete each request and increase the risk of human error during manual review and editing. Upgrading to an advanced redaction suite will allow personnel to process public record requests with greater accuracy and efficiency by leveraging automated and Al-assisted redaction tools. These capabilities dramatically reduce processing time, improve precision in redacting only the protected portions of an image or video, and provide a more reliable review workflow. This upgrade will enable the department to provide more timely and accurate releases of public records while reducing staff hours spent on redaction, minimizing errors or omissions, and strengthening overall compliance with public records and disclosure requirements. 24

At present, officers would physically need to be in or return to in their patrol vehicles if they wish to review call details, search/run information, update their own statuses, or review incident history. This limitation creates delays, especially during foot patrols, community interactions, special events, and incidents occurring away from the vehicle. A mobile CAD application solution removes these barriers by making CAD functionality accessible anywhere in the field. Justification: Implementing a Mobile CAD application will substantially improve officer efficiency, situational awareness, and overall operational performance. Officers will be able to access real-time CAD data from any location, receive instant call updates that enhance response times and reduce radio traffic, update their status directly from their phones, and review premise history, hazards, BOLOs, and other patrol unit’s locations without needing to return to their vehicles. Mobile CAD is becoming a standard across regional law enforcement agencies, reflecting the operational reality that officers frequently work in dynamic environments where immediate access to information is critical. A mobile CAD platform provides continuous access to essential data and improves operational resilience. Adopting this technology is a necessary modernization step that enhances mobility, officer safety, and department-wide efficiency. This capability will align our agency with current industry practices and equip our personnel with the tools needed to operate effectively in today’s fast-paced field environment. records.text: The Senior Building Inspector FTE plays a critical role in the Building Services Division by supporting large-scale and complex development projects, including apartment communities, industrial facilities, data centers, and commercial centers. The expertise and attention to detail required at this level are essential for making on-site evaluations and determinations and for providing support to the Chief and Deputy Building Officials. The Building Inspection team currently consists of two Senior Building Inspectors G12 and two Building Inspectors G10. One of the incumbent Building Inspectors has the experience and skillset necessary to perform at the Senior level. Given the ongoing and upcoming inspections associated with multiple apartment developments and three major data center projects, a third Senior Building Inspector is warranted. During the first six months as a Building Inspector, the incumbent Alex Rodriguez has consistently demonstrated the knowledge, leadership, and technical expertise expected of a Senior Building Inspector. His performance shows a strong grasp of complex construction processes, proactive problem-solving, and the ability to manage high-volume, high-impact projects with minimal oversight. In addition, Alex has assumed increased inspection responsibilities to support the Building Inspection team, particularly in overseeing large- scale multi-family developments, tenant improvements (Tls), and new commercial construction. These assignments are critical to advancing the City’s development progress and require a comprehensive understanding of building code compliance, construction phases, and effective coordination with contractors and design teams. Alex supports the team by inspecting residential projects as well as assigned commercial projects, which have increased with the amount of new construction underway. Alex supports and coaches the other Building Inspector on single-family residential project inspections. He also inspects commercial multi-family residential developments and commercial retail projects. Alex played a key role in the V-Townhomes at Encanto residential townhome development. He successfully maintained inspection timelines, ensured building code compliance, and collaborated closely with site supervisors and contractors to resolve issues proactively. Through consistent communication and coordination with the applicant, he supported the issuance of numerous Certificates of Occupancy on an accelerated schedule for a high-demand developer. Currently, Alex oversees inspections for The Stately — Ascent at Fairway, a large multi-family residential apartment development with several hundred units under construction at a fast pace. Alex oversaw both the shell building and tenant improvement inspections for a new Starbucks building, demonstrating his ability to manage multiple stages of construction and his comprehensive understanding of building systems from core construction through final occupancy. He is also responsible for inspections on a new Dunkin’ building with a drive-through and an adjacent inline shop building with two restaurants and a drive-through. Alex performs beyond those projects typically assigned to a Building Inspector given his many years of inspection experience. Alex has consistently completed his regular inspection assignments with accuracy and professionalism. This demonstrates his ability to manage an increased workload while maintaining the quality and timeliness expected of the department. His successful handling of complex projects further underscores his readiness to advance into the role of Senior Building Inspector. Alex's attention to detail, ability to identify and resolve code issues in the field, and collaborative approach with both internal staff and external partners are qualities highly valued at the senior level. To meet departmental operational needs and retain this high-performing employee, the department recommends reclassifying this position to Senior Building Inspector. 73

records.text: According to the U.S. Census Bureau's 2024 estimates, there are approximately 59.3 million Americans aged 65 and over, accounting for 17.7% of the total U.S. population. The Population Reference Bureau (PRB) reports that the senior population stood at 58 million in 2022, and is projected to reach 82 million by 2050, representing a 47% increase over three decades. According to the National Council in Aging, over 19 million (45%) older adult households do not have the income needed to cover basic living costs based on cost-of-living data. Seniors who live in poverty are an especially vulnerable group due to increased physical limitations, medical needs and social isolation. Therefore, our Senior Services plays a key role in providing vital services and opportunities that will improve the health, social interaction and quality of life for our growing senior adult population while prolonging independence that allows for seniors to stay in their homes longer. Senior Services has experienced a significant increase in meal service, transportation, food distribution, and activity offerings. A comparison of utilization data from FY2024 to anticipated FY2026 attendance demonstrates significant increases as follows: number of congregate meals served has increased by 21%, number of home delivered meals served has increased 5%, transportation services has increased 13%, and supplemental food distribution has increased by 28%. The activity calendar has been revised to increase daily activity offerings by 25%, offering a variety of new activities, trips, and resources for the senior participants. As our senior adult population continues to grow, Senior Services anticipates a continued increase in demand for these essential services. It is also important to note that best practices indicate a staff to senior ratio of approximately 1:8 — 1:12 as ideal . Currently, Avondale Senior Services program staff is operating at a ratio of 1 Regular FTE for every 14.5 seniors including the temporary Part time Coordinator positions. In order to meet the current and anticipated growth, these positions are necessary to support the day-to-day operations, including supervision of staff and expansion of programming. Not funding these positions will impede the city's ability to meet the increasing demand for services for our vulnerable senior population. HR Reviewed? Ongoing: $0 One-Time: $0 Total: $0 Council Goal: — Innovative and Effective Government Description: $15,843 to be used for an ADA compliant PDF Remediation tool. The program will help the City ensure compliance with WCAG ADA Title II minimum standards while providing equal access to online information for residents with disabilities, including those who are blind, have low vision, or have motor impairments and rely on assistive technology. Justification: This technology automatically remediates accessibility issues by converting PDFs into accessible, html formats, generating alt text for images, and providing accessible transcripts so documents can be easily used with screen readers. The platform also offers accessibility insights and recommendations to help staff identify and correct issues before publishing. Without this tool, City staff would have to spend considerable time creating PDF documents that are ADA-accessible. This technology is being implemented as part of the new website redesign, and will be available across City departments. Additional features such as document language translation, live translator options, Al-powered summaries, and searchable topic menus within PDFs improve usability for all users and make it easier to locate and understand important information. This solution provides a simple, efficient way to improve accessibility, reduce manual staff workload, and ensure the City delivers inclusive digital services to the community. records.text: Asset Replacement Title: Lift Station Rehabilitation Program FY2028 and Beyond Project #: A0272 Department: Public Works Description: The program provides funding to maintain and upgrade the City’s existing wastewater lift stations. The program is designed to fund the rehabilitation of at least one site per year. Justification: Lift stations operate in a very corrosive environment where equipment damage and odor generation are constant. As these facilities age, the equipment needs replacement to ensure continued operations. The rehabilitation of each lift station could consist of pump/motor replacements, piping, appurtenances and instrumentation replacement/upgrade, generator repairs, and wet-well recoating. Public Works will continue to evaluate and prioritize the projects based on operational needs and facility conditions. The lift station rehabilitation program is part of the 2018 Integrated Utility Master Plan. records.text: Asset Replacement Title: Police Asset Replacement Program FY2028 and Beyond Project #: A0276 Department: Police Description: Asset replacement for police equipment encompasses the identification, evaluation, and replacement of critical tools and technologies that are essential for law enforcement operations. This includes, but is not limited to, firearms, body armor, vehicles, radios, surveillance equipment, and mobile data terminals. The replacement process will prioritize items that are outdated, deteriorating, or no longer meeting the department's needs due to technological advancements or changes in operational requirements. A comprehensive assessment of each asset's condition, performance, and serviceability will guide the selection of appropriate replacements, ensuring that all new equipment meets current standards for safety, functionality, and regulatory compliance. Justification: The replacement of outdated police equipment is essential for maintaining operational efficiency, ensuring officer safety, and upholding public trust. As technology advances, older equipment can become unreliable, less effective, or incompatible with newer systems, hindering law enforcement's ability to perform duties at the highest standard. Inadequate or malfunctioning gear poses significant risks to both officers and the public, including the potential for injury, delays in response time, and compromised investigations. Additionally, modern equipment is designed to improve overall performance, enhance communication capabilities, and ensure compliance with evolving regulations. Investing in the timely replacement of police equipment is not only a matter of safety but also a proactive strategy to foster public confidence and maintain a law enforcement agency's ability to protect and serve effectively. records.text: Asset Replacement Title: Police Asset Replacement Program FY2027 Project #: A0518 Department: Police Description: Asset replacement for police equipment encompasses the identification, evaluation, and replacement of critical tools and technologies that are essential for law enforcement operations. This includes, but is not limited to, ballistic vests, drones, firearms and accessories, and K9. The replacement process will prioritize items that are outdated, deteriorating, or no longer meeting the department's needs due to technological advancements or changes in operational requirements. A comprehensive assessment of each asset's condition, performance, and serviceability will guide the selection of appropriate replacements, ensuring that all new equipment meets current standards for safety, functionality, and regulatory compliance. Significant items for FY 2027 include: Handguns: $40,000 SWAT Vests: $40,000 Ballistic Vests: $38,000 Ballistic Shields: $36,000 Justification: The replacement of outdated police equipment is essential for maintaining operational efficiency, ensuring officer safety, and upholding public trust. As technology advances, older equipment can become unreliable, less effective, or incompatible with newer systems, hindering law enforcement's ability to perform duties at the highest standard. Inadequate or malfunctioning gear poses significant risks to both officers and the public, including the potential for injury, delays in response time, and compromised investigations. Additionally, modern equipment is designed to improve overall performance, enhance communication capabilities, and ensure compliance with evolving regulations. Investing in the timely replacement of police equipment is not only a matter of safety but also a proactive strategy to foster public confidence and maintain a law enforcement agency's ability to protect and serve effectively. records.text: Parks and Recreation Title: |§ Agua Fria Trailhead at Friendship Park and McDowell Rd (Formerly Recharge Project #: P0015 Park) Department: Parks, Recreation & Libraries Description: The initial scope of this project was to evaluate and design a possible expansion of Friendship Park north of McDowell Road utilizing COA and FCDMC land with the potential to add 70+ acres to the park system (48 developed), including unique riparian area utilizing existing recharge basins. The plan would help identify costs, which will be essential to pursuing grant opportunities. records.text: Parks and Recreation Title: | Base and Meridian Wildlife Area Restoration Project #: P0387 Department: Parks, Recreation & Libraries Description: In FY2023, water releases on the Salt River caused substantial damage to the Base and Meridian Wildlife area. This included damage to pathways, river launch points, signage, trails, and foliage. As a result, the area is no longer safe to conduct programming or host events such as the Tres Rios Nature Festival. Funds for this project would go toward repair of the low water ford and stabilization with grouted rip rap to minimize future erosions, and to improve approximately 1800 If of gravel surfacing both north and south of the low water ford to create a more level walking surface. The City of Avondale will work with AZ Game and Fish to make the repairs and that agency plans to restore the kayak launch. Total budget project: $1,300,000 Estimated completion: January 31, 2026 Operating impacts: Minimal. AZ Game and Fish owns and manages the land. Preparations for events may incur slight costs. Justification: The Base and Meridian wildlife area is a popular outdoor recreation site that receives thousands of visitors every year and in its current state is unable to support any programming such as events or other forms of outdoor recreation like hiking or canoeing in a safe capacity. To restore the site to a condition that allows for safe recreation opportunities, substantial repairs will need to be made. Should funding not be made available, it will delay the ability for the City to resume recreation programming at the space. The City applied for federal funding to support the project in the amount of $500,000. Work was originally scheduled to be performed in winter of 2024, but the opportunity to access outside funding warranted the delay. In addition, work cannot proceed between March and September to protect native bird nesting, but the project will be completed prior the 2026 Tres Rios Nature Festival allowing that event to return to this location. The FY26 request includes an additional $300,000 to cover the costs of the repairs. records.text: Parks and Recreation Title: Las Ligas Park Improvements Project #: P0473 Department: Parks, Recreation & Libraries Description: The Las Ligas Park Redevelopment will transform the existing 8.4-acre site by combining two parcels and delivering a comprehensive redesign that brings the park up to current standards while enhancing the overall user experience. Planned improvements include upgraded drainage, enhanced lighting and security features, renovated sports fields, updated fitness amenities, improved irrigation, and new landscaping. The project will also improve sidewalk connectivity, expand and upgrade parking areas, renovate the playground, and add a new restroom building. Additional enhancements include increasing the number of ramadas, installing security cameras (with quantities and locations to be finalized during design and coordinated with power and IT), and adding shade structures over sports courts, spectator areas, and play areas. Sports lighting will be incorporated for extended use, and new site furnishings, signage, and park monumentation will be added to meet PRLD standards and maintain consistency with other City parks. The project will require a ALTA, Exhibit, and Legal description and will be coordinated with the separate CIP project for the widening of Lower Buckeye Road. Total project budget: $14,000,000 Estimated Completion Date: June 2029 Updated estimated completion date: June 2032 Operating impacts: staff anticipates an increase to utilities, contractual landscape maintenance, and general repair and maintenance Justification: The Las Ligas Park Redevelopment will modernize an aging 8.4-acre neighborhood park and improve safety, accessibility, and recreational opportunities for the surrounding community. As available land for new parks becomes increasingly limited due to Avondale’s growth, maximizing the functionality and usability of existing park acreage is critical to meeting resident needs. The redevelopment will combine two parcels and redesign the site to create a more efficient and cohesive park layout, including upgraded sports fields, improved lighting, enhanced shade, updated irrigation and landscaping, and improved pedestrian access and amenities. These improvements will significantly enhance the user experience and support increased park usage. Overall, the redevelopment is a critical investment in community well-being, sustainability, and quality of life. It will revitalize a neighborhood park, provide safe and modern amenities, and support the growing recreational needs of the Avondale community. This project aligns with City priorities to invest in and revitalize neighborhood parks and is supported by the voter-approved Proposition 404. records.text: Title: —§ Agua Fria Trail Pedestrian Bridge North Landing Project #: P0509 Department: Parks, Recreation & Libraries Description: This project is located within the City of Avondale’s Friendship Park, situated between Interstate 10 (I-10) and McDowell Road, and includes the construction of the north pedestrian trail connection leading to the future pedestrian bridge over the Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT) drainage channel. The scope of work includes removals, earthwork, utility relocations, and construction of a multiuse path with associated amenities. Improvements also include extending electrical services to support lighting for both the trail and the planned pedestrian bridge, installation of security cameras, landscaping, and other ancillary site enhancements necessary to complete the connection to the forthcoming bridge project. In addition, the project will construct a pedestrian sidewalk loop around soccer fields #9 and #10 and provide new site furnishings at trail junction locations to support user comfort and wayfinding. Complete Budget: $469,000 Expected Completion Date: Sep 2027 Operating impacts: $5,000 for repair and maintenance Justification: The Friendship Park North Pedestrian Trail Connection project is a vital investment in improving multimodal accessibility, safety, and connectivity within one of Avondale’s most heavily used recreational destinations. By constructing this new trail segment, the City will establish a key link to the planned pedestrian bridge over the ADOT drainage channel, ultimately providing safe, uninterrupted access for pedestrians and cyclists traveling between areas north and south of Interstate 10. This improvement supports the community's increasing demand for walkable and bike-friendly infrastructure, reduces reliance on vehicular travel within the park, and enhances circulation for recreation users, youth sports participants, and residents. The project also replaces aging utilities, lighting infrastructure, and site amenities—significantly improving safety, visibility, and the overall user experience. Sidewalk enhancements around soccer fields #9 and #10 will further ease congestion and improve ADA accessibility for families and spectators. Importantly, the project leverages $500,000 in federal earmark funding for construction, minimizing the financial impact on the City while delivering substantial long-term public benefits. The trail connection also aligns with regional and local transportation goals, including MAG’s Bicycle and Pedestrian Program priorities. Completion of this segment is a crucial step toward advancing Avondale’s broader vision for a connected, accessible trail and pedestrian network across the community. records.text: Public Safety Title: —§ Training Tower Project #: S0398 Department: Fire and Medical Description: Budget would allow for demo of old fire tower structure and build of new modern, 3 story training tower that would facilitate live fire suppression simulation using liquid propane (LP) gas driven fires and a new modern 2 story clean burn building safe smoke simulation. Cost also includes flashover chamber training prop, car fire simulation prop, and trench rescue prop. Improvements also include replacing asphalt paving for more durable concrete paving, providing 2 new large shade canopies for shaded training outdoor classrooms, area for car extraction training, storage/compressor building for tower and burn building ventilation, site lighting, security cameras, & new secure access gate. These new facilities and site amenities will provide training for search and rescue, thermal imaging, and other training capabilities related to modern structural fire attack. Tower would also be used to support technical rope rescue training opportunities and other various training scenarios for Fire, Emergency Medical Services (EMS), and Law Enforcement training needs. The department's current training tower at the “Pit” training grounds has outlived its life expectancy. The upper-level floors and support structure are beginning to fail, and areas of the structure are no longer safe to use. records.text: Public Safety Title: | Assessment of Existing Public Safety Buildings Project #: $0513 Department: Office of Public Safety Description: This project involves conducting a comprehensive Facilities Condition Assessment (FCA) and Evaluation of Upgrades for the City’s Office of Public Safety, Fire and Medical, and Police Department facilities that were constructed prior to 2020 and have not undergone expansion or remodeling within the last five years. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the current condition, performance, and functionality of these facilities; identify necessary repairs, system upgrades, and building improvements; and determine the need for future remodels or facility enhancements to meet operational requirements. The assessment will examine architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, roofing, fire/life safety, accessibility, security, and site components to identify deficiencies, deferred maintenance, code compliance issues, and systems nearing end of life. The study will also assess building functionality, space utilization, operational efficiency, and the long-term suitability of each facility to support public safety operations. The findings from this FCA will provide the City with prioritized recommendations for immediate, mid-term, and long-term repairs and upgrades, along with cost estimates to inform future capital planning, maintenance strategies, and budgeting. The evaluation will also identify opportunities for modernization, energy efficiency improvements, accessibility compliance, and facility enhancements that support department growth and evolving service delivery needs. Deliverables will include comprehensive assessment reports, photographic documentation, deficiency logs, lifecycle analyses, and a consolidated summary to support decision-making and long-range facility planning. Proposed facilities and/or area of study are: Fire Station #173 — Includes assessment of converting an unused office area into workout space. Police & Fire Station #172 Police & Fire Station #174 Cashion Substation — Includes evaluation of potential expansion needs. Total project budget: $300,000 Estimated Completion: June 2029 Justification: Requesting a comprehensive Facilities Condition Assessment study for the Office of Public Safety, Fire, and Police buildings is essential for preserving their integrity, enhancing safety, ensuring effective operations, and planning for future needs. The findings will provide critical insights into repair, maintenance, and upgrade needs, which will help align these facilities with the evolving demands of public safety while maintaining fiscal responsibility. This study will be a cornerstone for informed decision-making regarding infrastructure investments and will contribute to the long-term sustainability of these vital public service buildings. Identified in IIP: — False Enhancement Category: Program Enhancement 354

records.text: Public Safety Title: Feasibility Study for Expansion of Courts Office Areas Project #: $0540 Department: City Court Description: This project involves a Feasibility and Programming Study to assess the current and future space needs of the Courts and determine the potential to expand the building footprint on both floors. The consultant will gather relevant information, evaluate the existing layout, and analyze current and projected space utilization. The study will explore options for reconfiguration, renovation, or expansion within or adjacent to the existing facility and identify any structural, operational, or site constraints. The consultant will identify applicable building code, accessibility, life safety, and security requirements, and assess the condition and capacity of existing building systems including HVAC, fire suppression, electrical panels, and emergency power/generator systems. Deficiencies related to code compliance, ADA accessibility, life safety, and security will be documented. For each feasible option, the consultant will provide order-of-magnitude cost estimates and an approximate implementation schedule. A final report summarizing findings, options, costs, and recommendations will be prepared for the City’s use. Estimated Project Budget: $100,000 Estimated Project Completion: June 2028 Operating impacts: No impacts Justification: The Courts facility is experiencing increased operational demands and evolving service requirements that may exceed the capacity of its current layout and available space. To ensure the building can continue to support efficient court operations, accommodate future growth, and meet modern standards for security, accessibility, and public service, the City requires a detailed evaluation of its space needs and expansion potential. A Feasibility and Programming Study will provide critical information on whether the building can be reconfigured, renovated, or expanded to meet long-term requirements. The study will identify deficiencies in building systems, code compliance, ADA accessibility, life safety features, and security provisions that may limit the facility's ability to support future operations. It will also assess the feasibility and cost implications of various renovation or expansion options, enabling the City to make informed decisions regarding capital investments. Without this study, the City risks underutilizing available space, making inefficient upgrades, or committing resources to improvements that may not meet long-term needs. The findings will guide responsible budgeting, project planning, and strategic development of the Courts facility to ensure it remains functional, safe, and capable of serving the community effectively. records.text: Transportation Title: | Van Buren Street Widening & Improvements - 107th Avenue to Avondale Project #: T0210 Boulevard Department: Engineering Services Description: This project includes the design and construction of roadway improvements to Van Buren Street between Avondale Boulevard and 107th Avenue, widening the corridor to provide two travel lanes in each direction. The improvements will include installation of vertical curb and gutter, sidewalks where appropriate, bike lanes, streetlights, conduit, a new pavement section, updated striping, and temporary retention basins with scuppers to manage stormwater. An existing Salt River Project (SRP) irrigation ditch within the project limits will be placed into underground piping to accommodate the widened roadway. Land acquisition will be required to obtain necessary right-of-way. These improvements will enhance roadway capacity, multimodal connectivity, and overall safety along this key east-west corridor. The existing roadway does not provide sufficient travel lanes or multimodal facilities to accommodate current and projected traffic volumes, resulting in congestion, operational delays, and limited mobility for pedestrians and cyclists. Widening the roadway to two lanes in each direction, along with adding curb and gutter, sidewalks, bike lanes, and modern streetlighting, will improve traffic flow, accessibility, and corridor safety. Stormwater infrastructure upgrades, including temporary retention basins and scuppers, are essential to manage runoff and reduce localized flooding. Undergrounding the existing SRP irrigation ditch is required to allow for the expanded roadway cross-section and to ensure long-term functionality. Right-of- way acquisition is necessary to support the full build-out of these improvements. Advancing this project will improve connectivity, support economic growth, and ensure the transportation network remains resilient and capable of meeting community needs. records.text: Transportation Title: — Traffic Signal - Fairway Drive and Corporate Drive Project #: T0248 Department: Engineering Services Description: This project involves the design and construction of a new traffic signal at the intersection of Fairway Drive and Corporate Drive. The work includes installing a fully operational traffic signal system using Maricopa County Department of Transportation (MCDOT)-style poles, a new signal cabinet, detection systems, conduit, wiring, and all associated hardware. Because the intersection is skewed, the signal layout and pole placement will be designed to account for the unique geometry while remaining within the existing right-of-way. In addition to the signal system, the project includes civil improvements such as pavement tapers, curb and gutter installation, and ADA-compliant curb ramps at the southwest corner of the intersection. A Traffic Signal Warrant Study, as defined by the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD), evaluates multiple intersection conditions such as vehicular volume, pedestrian volume, crash history, progression, and delay. This location will be monitored over time, and once it meets the applicable MUTCD criteria, the traffic signal design may be initiated. Implementing a traffic signal at this intersection will improve traffic flow, reduce delays along the arterial roadway network, and provide safer and more efficient access for vehicles entering and exiting adjacent neighborhood areas. Additionally, the project reflects the City’s commitment to providing timely infrastructure improvements in coordination with private development, with the Developer contributing to the project costs. records.text: Transportation Title: | Lower Buckeye Road Widening: Litchfield Road to 107th Avenue (formerly Project #: T0376 Lower Buckeye Corridor Study) Department: Engineering Services Description: This project will complete arterial widening of Lower Buckeye Road between Litchfield Road and the west bank of the Agua Fria River, and between South 127th Avenue and South 107th Avenue. These roadway segments are primarily limited to two travel lanes and no longer meet the capacity, safety, and multimodal needs of the community. The project will construct two continuous through lanes in each direction, install raised landscaped medians or a two- way center left-turn lane where appropriate, and provide left- and right-turn lanes at key locations to improve access and mobility. These improvements are critical to supporting increasing traffic volumes, enhancing corridor reliability, and preparing the roadway for anticipated growth associated with the future State Route 30 (SR-30). Lower Buckeye Road serves as an essential arterial route, providing connectivity to major regional and community destinations, including MC- 85, Phoenix- Goodyear Airport, Festival Fields Regional Park, the Central Avenue Historic Corridor, the Avondale Municipal Operations Service Center, the future Traffic and Parks Operations Facility, multiple schools, commercial areas, residential neighborhoods, and the multi-use path and trailhead system along the Agua Fria River. Portions of the corridor have been improved at key intersections—such as South El Mirage Road, South Avondale Boulevard, and South 107th Avenue—but the connecting roadway segments remain incomplete. Completing this project will close these infrastructure gaps and support full corridor build-out as envisioned in the City’s Transportation Master Plan. Project improvements will include bicycle lanes, ADA-compliant sidewalks, multi-use paths, upgraded street lighting, new landscaping and irrigation, and drainage facilities. The project will also include utility relocations, right-of-way acquisition, driveway reconstruction, and installation of Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) components to enhance safety and traffic operations. These investments will significantly increase roadway capacity, reduce congestion, improve multimodal safety, and support economic development by strengthening access to jobs, schools, services, and recreation. The project advances the City’s long-term goals of providing a safe, resilient, and connected transportation network while supporting the continued growth of the West Valley. Total City contribution: $18,152,000 Anticipated Off-setting Revenue: $7,000,000 Total project budget: $35,806,750 Estimated completion date: December 2029 Justification: 393

records.text: The justification for moving forward with the Lower Buckeye Road arterial widening project is strengthened by the City of Avondale’s recent award of $25,064,725 in federal funding, which provides a significant portion of the resources needed to advance this critical infrastructure investment. This funding supports the timely construction of improvements necessary to address existing congestion, safety challenges, and multimodal deficiencies along the corridor. Lower Buckeye Road is a key arterial route serving rapidly growing residential neighborhoods, employment centers, schools, parks, and regional destinations, and its current two-lane configuration is inadequate for increasing traffic demand and future development. The widening project will also play a vital role in supporting traffic flow associated with the future State Route 30 (SR-30), which is expected to generate substantial east-west travel demand throughout the area. Enhancing corridor capacity now will reduce pressure on the transportation network once SR-30 is constructed and ensure smooth, reliable access to adjacent communities and regional facilities. The project improvements will enhance mobility, improve emergency response reliability, reduce crash risks, and provide safe and accessible facilities for pedestrians and bicyclists. Leveraging the federal grant enables the City to deliver long-planned improvements, close missing infrastructure gaps, and support the long-term build-out of the transportation network as identified in the City’s Transportation Master Plan. This investment ensures that Avondale remains well-positioned to accommodate growth, strengthen economic vitality, and improve overall quality of life for residents and visitors as the region continues to develop. records.text: Transportation Title: © Dysart Road/McDowell Road Intersection Project #: T0405 Department: Engineering Services Description: This project will design and construct improvements to the Dysart Road/McDowell Road intersection with dual left turn lanes. The proposed improvements will increase the left turn storage northbound and southbound to accommodate the traffic by implementing longer storage lengths and dual left turn bays. The existing traffic signal including the hardware will be replaced to accommodate the widening. The project will consist of a two phase approach with the widening of the north/south bound lanes (Phase |) by modifying the traffic signal and widening of the median on the southside of McDowell in phase 1. Phase 2 will consist of the widening on the east/west lanes. Total project budget: $3,540,000 Original estimated completion: June 2026 Updated estimated completion: December 2028 Operating impacts: Striping every 3-5 years depending on vehicle volumes, signage, road maintenance, Electric Justification: The intersection of Dysart Road and McDowell Road is a high-volume, critical arterial junction that experiences significant congestion, particularly in the northbound and southbound left-turn movements. Existing left-turn storage is inadequate to meet current and projected traffic demand, resulting in long queues that spill into through lanes and undermine overall intersection efficiency and safety. The proposed improvements will incorporate recommendations from the Road Safety Assessment conducted by the Maricopa Association of Governments (MAG), ensuring that the design addresses documented safety concerns and operational deficiencies. The project will construct dual left-turn lanes in both directions, providing longer storage lengths and increasing intersection capacity. These dual lefts will improve traffic flow, reduce crashes and delays, and provide safer access for vehicles entering and exiting adjacent developments. The two-phase construction approach—first widening the north-south lanes while modifying the traffic signal and median on the south side of McDowell Road, followed by widening on the east-west approaches—allows the improvements to be delivered efficiently while minimizing traffic disruption. Overall, these enhancements will improve safety, reduce congestion, and support continued mobility and economic growth along this vital transportation corridor. records.text: Transportation Title: — Traffic Signal - 116th Ave and McDowell Project #: T0408 Department: Engineering Services Description: This project includes the design and construction of a new traffic signal at the intersection of 116th Avenue and McDowell Road, a key connection serving growing residential and commercial areas. The signal will utilize rectangular, cocoa brown double mast arms and poles in a trombone-style configuration consistent with City standards. The design phase will include evaluation of existing road geometry, traffic volumes, lighting, pedestrian activity, and turning movements to determine the most effective signal layout. Design considerations may include signal timing, lane configurations, turn lanes, pedestrian crossings, and required adjustments to the intersection. The construction phase will involve installation of traffic signal poles and mast arms, signal heads, controllers, electrical and communication wiring, pavement markings, and any necessary modifications to the existing intersection layout to ensure full operational functionality and safety compliance. The completed traffic signal will improve traffic flow, enhance safety, and increase accessibility for vehicles and pedestrians traveling through the intersection. Total project budget: $1,200,000 Estimated completion: December 2025 Updated Estimated completion: December 2026 Operating impacts: Electrical cost, Painting every 10 years, Repair and Maintenance (bulbs, lens, battery back cameras, pre-emption equipment, push buttons) Justification: A traffic signal at the intersection of 116th Avenue and McDowell Road is necessary to enhance safety, improve operational efficiency, and accommodate ongoing development in the surrounding area. As traffic volumes and turning movements continue to increase, the existing intersection configuration creates delays and elevates the risk of collisions, particularly during peak travel periods. A fully signalized intersection will provide controlled movements for vehicles and pedestrians, reducing conflict points and improving predictability for all users. The installation of rectangular, cocoa brown double mast arms in a trombone-style configuration ensures consistency with City standards and supports long- term durability and maintainability. Implementing this traffic signal will improve pedestrian access, support multimodal connectivity, and enhance corridor reliability as growth continues along McDowell Road. Overall, the project supports the City’s commitment to safe and efficient transportation infrastructure while preparing the corridor for future demand. records.text: Transportation Title: | Safety Action and Demonstration Plan Project #: T0416 Department: Engineering Services Description: This project engages a consultant to develop a comprehensive Safety Action and Demonstration Plan for the City. The plan will identify roadway safety hazards, analyze crash trends, and establish defined goals and strategies to reduce accidents and improve overall transportation safety. Work will include data collection, stakeholder engagement, development of recommended countermeasures, and preparation of demonstration projects to test and validate safety improvements. The plan will serve as a guiding framework for future investment decisions and implementation efforts. This project will be partially funded through grant resources. Total project budget: $700,000 Estimated completion date: October 2027 Operating impact: Justification: The City does not currently have a Safety Action Plan or Demonstration Plan, both of which are essential tools for systematically identifying roadway safety risks and implementing effective countermeasures. Establishing these plans will allow the City to modernize its policies and procedures, create a consistent safety-focused culture, and proactively reduce identified hazards for all roadway users. A formal Safety Action and Demonstration Plan will also position the City to make data-driven decisions, prioritize investments, and pursue additional federal funding opportunities for safety improvements. This project is partially grant-funded, reducing the financial impact on the City while enabling development of a comprehensive, high-quality plan. The City has been awarded a Federal Safe Streets for All (SS4A) Grant in the amount of $560,000, with a required City match of $140,000, for a total project cost of $700,000. Utilizing this funding to develop a Safety Action and Demonstration Plan will support long-term safety outcomes, improve operational consistency across departments, and enhance the overall well-being of the community. records.text: Transportation Title: © McDowell Bridge Lighting Project #: T0507 Department: Engineering Services Description: This project includes the design and installation of lighting on the McDowell Road bridge over the Agua Fria River. The proposed lighting system is anticipated to consist of solar-powered fixtures mounted directly onto the existing bridge structure. Because the McDowell Road bridge was not originally constructed with features to accommodate lighting—unlike the nearby Van Buren bridge—modifications to the structure will be required. These modifications are expected to be superficial or non-structural; however, the extent of necessary adjustments will be evaluated during design. The preferred approach is to install streetlights of sufficient height and strength to illuminate both the pedestrian sidewalk on the north side of the bridge and the four vehicular travel lanes. If structural limitations prevent installation of full-height roadway lighting, the project may provide smaller-scale lighting focused on the pedestrian facilities to avoid costly structural retrofits. The scope of work will include structural assessment, lighting design, fixture selection, solar power integration, mounting hardware design, and construction. records.text: Transportation Title: | Dysart Road Intersection Improvements at I-10 to Rancho Santa Fe Project #: T0544 Department: Engineering Services Description: This project involves the design of roadway and intersection capacity improvements along Dysart Road from I-10 to approximately 500 feet north of Rancho Santa Fe Boulevard and associated right-of-way (ROW). The work will address existing and future traffic demands by widening the corridor and enhancing turning movements at the Dysart Road/Rancho Santa Fe intersection. Improvements include extending the northbound deceleration lane further south toward the I-10 interchange, constructing dual northbound left-turn lanes, and lengthening storage areas to accommodate increased traffic volumes. The project will also add a dedicated westbound right-turn deceleration lane and extend the existing dual westbound left-turn lanes to improve intersection efficiency. Implementation will require right-of-way acquisition, utility relocations, and restoration of affected private properties. In addition, the existing traffic signal system—including poles, mast arms, signal heads, and associated hardware—will be replaced and upgraded to support the widened intersection configuration. Existing roadway and intersection configurations are insufficient to accommodate current and projected traffic, resulting in congestion, long queues, and delayed travel times—particularly during peak commuting hours and near the I-10 interchange. Extending the northbound deceleration lane, constructing dual northbound left-turn lanes, and providing longer storage lengths will significantly improve traffic flow and reduce queue spillback toward the freeway. Similarly, adding a westbound right-turn deceleration lane and extending dual westbound left-turn lanes will enhance intersection efficiency and reduce conflict points. Replacing and upgrading the traffic signal system is essential to support the widened intersection and ensure safe and reliable operations. The project also requires right-of-way acquisition, utility relocation, and private property restoration to facilitate the necessary improvements. Overall, this project will enhance mobility, improve safety, reduce congestion, and support continued economic development and growth within the surrounding area. records.text: Utilities Title: | Sediment Removal - Crystal Gardens & McDowell Recharge Basins Project #: U0340 Department: Public Works Description: This project is for the removal of excess sediment in Crystal Gardens Wetlands and scraping and removal from the recharge basins at the McDowell Recharge Facility. The project includes the dredging and hauling to a permitted disposal site approximately 12,000 cubic yards of sediment and bio solids material from cells 1A, 10A, 8B, and 14B in Crystal Gardens lakes over a 3-year period. Total project budget: $2,050,000 Original estimated completion: January 2025 Updated estimated completion: October 2026 Justification: The Crystal Gardens Wetlands treats water from the Salt River Project (SRP) canal before it is recharged into the underground aquifer for future use. Over time, sediment has built up in several of the treatment cells resulting in reduced efficiency of the system and making routine maintenance challenging. Currently, some treatment cells have sediment levels that exceed 10 feet in depth. Excess sediment creates anaerobic conditions that can be unhealthy for aquatic life, produce a foul odor, appear unsightly as it approaches the surface, and can be unsafe for staff to maintain normally. Removal of excess sediment is necessary for proper function of the Crystal Gardens Wetlands facility. At the McDowell Recharge Facility, scraping and removing fine-grain sediment and organic matter from the bottom of the recharge basins is a routine maintenance activity performed as needed to maintain proper infiltration rates and optimize the City's recharge capability. records.text: Utilities Title: Well Electrical Equipment Upgrades Project #: U0479 Department: Public Works Description: Public Works (Water Production & Treatment Division) is requesting $1,250,000 for electrical upgrades at Well 10, Well 11, and Well 12. This project encompasses the design and construction necessary to replace or upgrade outdated electrical equipment, ensuring a more reliable, robust, and safer operation. The project includes $250,000 for design and $300,000 per site for construction, with a $100,000 contingency. Total Project Budget: $1,250,000 Completion Date: June 30, 2027 Updated Completion Date: October 1, 2027 Operating Impacts: None anticipated. Justification: A condition assessment by Carollo determined that the Motor Control Center (MCC) equipment at these sites is nearing the end of its useful life. Operations teams are already encountering periodic electrical failures and malfunctions, underscoring the urgency of this project. These wells are critical to supplying water to the Rancho Santa Fe Booster Station, a major component of our water delivery system. Upgrading this infrastructure will enhance reliability, prevent operational disruptions, and ensure a consistent water supply for the community. records.text: Utilities Title: | New Modular Building at Coldwater Booster Station Project #: U0480 Department: Public Works Description: Public Works (Water Production & Treatment) is requesting $375,000 to purchase and install a new modular building at the City’s Coldwater Booster Pump Station. This modular building will serve as office space for the Water Production & Treatment team, supporting their operational needs and enhancing their workspace efficiency. Total Project Budget: $375,000 Completion Date: June 30, 2026 Operating Impacts: Building operating expenses such as electricity, water, and contract maintenance for building/grounds. Justification: In FY24, Public Works requested $1,500,000 for a permanent Water Production & Treatment building to address the critical need for dedicated operator space. However, due to budget constraints in FY25, the project was removed from the capital outlay plan. To meet the ongoing need for operator workspace, the department proposes a cost-effective solution: purchasing and installing a modular office building at the Coldwater Booster Pump Station for $350,000. This modular office will provide a centralized workspace for the Water Production & Treatment staff (8), who currently operate out of multiple locations with limited space. It will enhance operational efficiencies, support Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) monitoring of wells, booster stations, and treatment facilities, and include permitting, furnishings, and other site needs. The modular unit can also be repurposed or sold in the future if a permanent solution is developed, making it a flexible and fiscally responsible investment. records.text: Utilities Title: Bartlett Dam Project Project #: U0481 Department: Public Works Description: Public Works (Water Resources) is requesting $15,000,000 to purchase additional water supplies from the Verde River Sediment Mitigation Project, also known as the Bartlett Dam Project. Total Project Budget: $15,000,000 Estimated Completion Date: June 30, 2030 Operating Impacts: None anticipated. Justification: Public Works (Water Resources) is requesting $23,000,000 to secure additional water supplies through the Verde River Sediment Mitigation Project, commonly known as the Bartlett Dam Project. This initiative is a strategic investment in the City’s long-term water security and resource sustainability, aligning with the City’s growth and expansion needs. Through this shared investment in the reconstruction of Bartlett Dam, the City is projected to receive approximately 5,000 acre-feet of additional water annually. While exact allocations are pending federal review, Avondale's share of the cost is anticipated to be approximately $23,000,000. This critical investment will enhance the City’s water supply resilience, ensuring adequate resources to meet increasing demands. By participating in this regional effort, Avondale demonstrates its commitment to proactive water resource management, collaboration, and sustainable growth. records.text: Utilities Title: Lift Station Flow Meter Purchase and Installation Project #: U0482 Department: Public Works Description: Public Works (Wastewater Collections) is requesting $500,000 to purchase and install flow meters at 8 lift stations. The City’s lift stations currently have flow meters installed at only 9 of the 17 stations operated and maintained by City staff. Flow meters are essential for accurately tracking flows, optimizing pumping efficiency, identifying inflow and infiltration (I&l) issues, addressing capacity concerns, and providing early warnings of system or equipment failures. Total Project Budget: $500,000 Completion Date: June 30, 2026 Operating Impacts: Future maintenance of these flow meters will be incorporated into ongoing operational expenditures. Justification: Without sufficient flow meters, staff must rely on pump run times, which is an imprecise method with too many variables to accurately pinpoint specific issues. This project will address the gap by installing or replacing flow meters at a minimum of 8 additional lift stations, significantly improving monitoring and operational efficiency. The estimated cost for this critical infrastructure upgrade is $500,000, ensuring a timely and effective solution for improved system performance and reliability. records.text: Utilities Title: | New Water Distribution Valve Exerciser Project #: U0483 Department: Public Works Description: Public Works (Water Distribution) is requesting a new valve exercise skid unit mounted on a 2024 4x2 super-duty chassis cab with a 12-foot flatbed. Both items are interdependent. The City's water distribution system contains over 8,430 valves, with this number growing as new developments are added. Regular maintenance, including vacuuming valve boxes and exercising each valve every 18 months, is essential to ensure the reliability of our water infrastructure. Properly functioning water valves are essential for controlling water flow throughout the distribution system, directly supporting the resilience of our infrastructure. records.text: Utilities Title: © PFAS Treatment Facility - Land & Design Project #: U0484 Department: Public Works Description: Public Works (Water Production & Treatment) is requesting $18,000,000 to address PFAS (Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances) mitigation requirements. The funds will support the acquisition of additional real estate essential for future treatment operations and the preliminary design and engineering necessary for construction. Total Project Budget: $18,000,000 Estimated completion: June 2028 Updated Completion Date: June 30, 2031 Justification: This project is critical to meeting federal and state compliance mandates for PFAS mitigation, ensuring the City adheres to the July 1, 2027, deadline to begin constructing treatment infrastructure. Investing $18 million now will enable the acquisition of necessary real estate and support the design phase, positioning the City to meet its regulatory obligations and avoid significant penalties while safeguarding public health and water quality. To support PFAS treatment operations, the City anticipates purchasing approximately 30,600 square feet of land near Northside Booster Pump Station, 122,000 square feet near future Well #27, and 7,650 square feet near Well #20. These acquisitions, estimated at $2.8 million, are critical to securing the space required for constructing the treatment facilities. Additionally, design costs for the PFAS treatment infrastructure are projected at 10% of the total construction budget, equating to approximately $15.2 million. Together, these investments lay the groundwork for a robust and effective solution to meet compliance requirements, protect water quality, and ensure the City's ability to provide safe drinking water for residents. records.text: Utilities Title: © Small Diameter Sewer Line Repair FY2027 Project #: U0534 Department: Public Works Description: The project scope is for the rehabilitation of approximately 5,000 linear feet (LF) of deteriorating Small Diameter Sanitary Sewer Lines (SDSS) (6-in, 8-in, 10-in, 12-in) by using methods of Cured-in-Place pipe (CIPP) lining, rehabilitation of 10 deteriorating manholes (MHs) by inserting a composite insert, and approximately 20 MH bench repair and point of repairs that were identified in the comprehensive condition assessment of its gravity sewer mains with diameters of 12 inches or smaller in June 2021. records.text: RESOLUTION NO. 1029-0526 A RESOLUTION OF THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AVONDALE, ARIZONA, SETTING FORTH THE TENTATIVE BUDGET AND ESTABLISHING THE EXPENDITURE LIMITATION FOR THE CITY OF AVONDALE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-2027. WHEREAS, pursuant to the provisions of the laws of the State of Arizona and the City Charter, the Council of the City of Avondale (the “City Council’) is required to adopt a budget; and WHEREAS, in accordance with ARIZ. REV. STAT. § 42-17102, the City Manager has prepared and filed with the City Council the City Manager’s Budget estimates for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2027; and WHEREAS, pursuant to the Arizona Constitution Article IX, Section 20, the city’s expenditure limitation for Fiscal Year 2026-2027 is $514,304,500; and NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AVONDALE as follows: SECTION 1. The recitals above are hereby incorporated as if fully set forth herein. SECTION 2. The statements and schedules attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference are hereby adopted as the City’s official tentative budget for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, and ending June 30, 2027. SECTION 3. Upon approval of the City Council, the City Manager or designee shall publish in the official City newspaper once per week for two consecutive weeks (i) the official tentative budget and (ii) a notice of the public hearing of the City Council to hear taxpayers and make tax levies at designated times and places. The notice shall include the physical addresses of the Avondale Civic Center Library, the Sam Garcia Western Avenue Library and the Avondale City Hall, and the website where the tentative budget may be found. Ifa truth in taxation notice is required under ARIZ. REV. STAT. § 42-17107, it may be combined with such hearing notice. SECTION 4. The City Manager or designee shall, no later than seven business days following consideration of this Resolution by the City Council, make available at the Avondale Civic Center Library, the Sam Garcia Western Avenue Library and the Avondale City Hall a complete copy of the tentative budget, and shall post the tentative budget on the City’s website. 3

records.title: City of Avondale FY2027 Tentative Budget
records.text: Tentative Budget Summary The FY2027 Tentative Budget continues to show the City of Avondale’s commitment to providing high-quality services to residents, businesses, and visitors in a fiscally sustainable manner. The FY2027 Tentative Budget is balanced, with revenues and resources greater than planned expenditures. The General Fund, which provides the funding for the majority of services and employees in the city, is structurally balanced in FY2027, with ongoing revenues greater than ongoing expenses. Per State Statute, the Tentative Budget sets the expenditure limit for FY2027. The budget may be reduced or reallocated, but the total budget adopted by City Council cannot be increased from the adopted Tentative Budget. The following graphs show the composition of theFY2027 Tentative Budget. Capital Outlay continues to be the largest category of expenditures at $205.5 million followed by $85.1 million in General Government expenditures. FY2027 Budget Expenses - All Funds- $514.3M @ Capital Outlay | $205.5M (40%) @ General Government | $85.1M (17%) @ Public Safety | $82.2M (16%) @ Utilities | $45.9M (9%) @ Contingency | $36.8M (7%) @ Community Services | $23.2M (5%) @ Debt | $20.9M (4%) @ Community & Economic Develop | $14.8M (3%) The graph above shows the $514.3 million proposed FY2027 Tentative Budget by function. The largest portion of the FY2027 budget is Capital Improvement at $205.5 million. $112..6 million of that budget is carryover of projects from the FY2026 budget. The City’s operating budget is $251.2 million in total, not including contingency, debt service, or transfers. 27

On-going revenues are projected to be equal to or greater than on-going expenses in FY2027. The on-going balance is considered when staff recommends supplemental requests for funding. A full list of recommended Supplemental Requests can be found in Appendix A. The Financial Policies of the city state that the city should maintain a structural balance, where on-going revenues are equal to or greater than on-going expenses in the General Fund. Ongoing expenses are currently projected to exceed ongoing revenues in FY2028 by $2.4 million, FY2029 by $2.3 million, and FY2030 by $370,000 due to the loss of ongoing Residential Rental Sales Tax revenues, which began in January 2025, and the implementation of the state’s flat income tax. The flat income tax reduces Urban Revenue Sharing revenues. The General Fund is expected to recover in FY2031 with ongoing revenues once again exceeding ongoing revenues due to expected increases in Sales Tax (TPT) revenues from the expected opening of multiple data centers in the City. The City will continue to monitor the projected forecast and will work towards balancing FY2028, FY2029, and FY2030. 30

records.text: The next graph shows the General Fund balance above the stabilization and capital reserve amounts. The stabilization amount is equal to 35% of adopted budgeted General Fund expenditures from the prior year, excluding interfund transfers and contingency appropriation. This reserve amount can be utilized to mitigate the impact of disasters, address emergency situations, and sudden or unexpected declines of revenues. The Capital Reserve amount is equal to $5 million and is available for unexpected increases in the costs of capital projects. The city is planning to spend the accumulated balance over these reserve amounts on capital projects, reinvesting the city’s resources into the city. A full list of included capital projects in the Tentative Budget can be found in Appendix B. 32
